chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from al-Sakuni from Ja'far from his father from Ali (peace be upon him)
Regarding the woman who commits zina (fornication/adultery) before being entered into by her husband, he said: 'They are separated, and she has no dowry, because the act was from her side.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's dowry if she commits zina before marriage consummation?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq establishes that pre-consummation adultery by the wife constitutes a fundamental defect (‘ayb) attributable to her, thereby justifying the forfeiture of her dowry (sadaq) upon separation. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the principle that the husband’s right to consummation is a primary condition of the marriage contract, and its absence due to the wife’s fault negates her financial claim. The chain of transmission highlights the direct link to the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing the authority of Imami legal reasoning in family law matters.
